subject: mathematics
title: Area Detectives
objective: Solve simple problems about the area of squares and rectangles using length × width.
introduction: A garden is 4 units long and 3 units wide. How many square units of soil will Milo plant?

items.prompt: A rectangle is 4 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its area?
items.explanation: Area = length × width = 4 × 3 = 12 square units. The distance around is perimeter, and 4 cm is only one side.

items.prompt: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 2 cm wide. What is its area?

options.text: a 5 by 2 rectangle has 10 square units

items.prompt: A square has sides of 3 cm. Why is its area 9 square units?

options.text: a square has equal side lengths

items.explanation: A square has equal sides, so area = side × side = 3 × 3 = 9 square units.

items.prompt: How can you check that a 4 by 3 rectangle has area 12?

options.text: counting unit squares checks the answer

items.explanation: Count the unit squares inside: 4 rows of 3 squares is 12 squares, which checks length × width.

items.prompt: Milo makes a 6 m by 2 m flower bed. What is its area?
items.explanation: Area is length × width: 6 m × 2 m = 12 square meters. The other choices add, measure around, or count corners.
